UPSTREAM: media: staging/intel-ipu3-v4l: reduce kernel stack usage The v4l2_pix_format_mplane structure is too large to be put on the kernel stack, as we can see in 32-bit builds: drivers/staging/media/ipu3/ipu3-v4l2.c: In function 'imgu_fmt': drivers/staging/media/ipu3/ipu3-v4l2.c:753:1: error: the frame size of 1028 bytes is larger than 1024 bytes [-Werror=frame-larger-than=] By dynamically allocating this array, the stack usage goes down to an acceptable 272 bytes for the same x86-32 configuration. BACKPORT: media: staging/intel-ipu3: parameter buffer refactoring Current ImgU driver processes and releases the parameter buffer immediately after queued from user. This does not align with other image buffers which are grouped in sets and used for the same frame. If user queues multiple parameter buffers continuously, only the last one will take effect. To make consistent buffers usage, this patch changes the parameter buffer handling and group parameter buffer with other image buffers for each frame. Each time driver will queue one more group of buffers when previous frame processed and buffers consumed by css. Signed-off-by: Tianshu Qiu <tian.shu.qiu@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Bingbu Cao <bingbu.cao@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+samsung@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit 8ecc7c9da013e702aa889002e1288521d7533293 git://linuxtv.org/media_tree.git master) BUG=b:139647343 TEST=Sanity checked basic camera functions. arc: networkd: Move setup and teardown logic into ArcService. This patch refactors the setup/teardown, init/uninit and enable/disable code from ArcIpConfig into ArcService. Earlier attempts to break each logical unit into multicle CLs caused too many problems given the timing and interconencted nature of these pieces, due largely to the fact that the functionality was beig split across processes. Another key change in this patch is the gating of enable/disable on both sides of the veth pair being up. This is achieved by DeviceManager listening to rt netlink messages on the host and ArcService doing the same in the container's net namespace. Doing so, guarantees that once IPv6 route detection and address assignment runs, it can set up the datapath and configuration immediately. One caveat here is that the device keeps state that is currently specific to the ARC guest alone. This will have to be expanded, if necessary, to accomodate others. More functionality is moved into Datapath from ArcIpConfig. In order to add DeviceManager unit testing, a base class was added for mocking. ArcIpConfig unit test removed since it is no longer relevant. FROMGIT: firmware: google: check if size is valid when decoding VPD data The VPD implementation from Chromium Vital Product Data project used to parse data from untrusted input without checking if the meta data is invalid or corrupted. For example, the size from decoded content may be negative value, or larger than whole input buffer. Such invalid data may cause buffer overflow. To fix that, the size parameters passed to vpd_decode functions should be changed to unsigned integer (u32) type, and the parsing of entry header should be refactored so every size field is correctly verified before starting to decode.
